## Responsibilities and public interface

Web consumers use the public core interface in packages/core/index.ts (also exported as @shop/core). Storage access and the order list belong to core; web routes may forward the public postOrder function. Core implementation modules may import core storage. The native static dependency graph must be acyclic. No boundary or cycle exceptions are accepted.

For example, a web consumer can use the public interface without importing storage:

```ts
import { servicePrice, postOrder } from '@shop/core'
export async function checkout(url: string, quantity = 1) {
  return postOrder(quantity, await servicePrice(url))
}
```

The controlled HTTP endpoint in journey.mjs supplies price 10; checkout must return { status: 201, total: 10 } for the default quantity. Public quote() continues to return 12. The existing quantity calculation is retained; no new business discount is introduced. Receipt wording is outside this correction.

## Checks and completion evidence

Install the locked development dependencies with npm ci using Node 24 or later. Run npm run check: TypeScript, unit tests, native boundaries and the real local HTTP journey must all pass. package.json owns the commands; boundaries.mjs owns static import/export resolution and cycle detection. The boundary check does not cover dynamic imports or every transitive facade leak; review new dependency syntax against the public-interface rule.

Acceptance cases live in this design, unit.test.mjs and journey.mjs. A change is complete when its affected journeys pass on the final inputs and authoritative-source impacts have been reviewed. Passing unit tests alone does not establish journey completion. For structural changes, capture passing public compatibility checks before and after; for bug fixes, retain the original failing reproduction and the final passing outcome. No hosted CI or delivery service is selected.

## Maintenance contract and portable assessment

.bstack/project.json maps paths to these rules and to DESIGN.md, glossary.md and AGENTS.md. For every change, compare against an explicit ancestor commit, inspect the diff and assess every mapped document and unmapped path. Record changed behavior, changed paths, a substantive reason, literal base/current source citations and any dependent work. Use updated with the actual before/after excerpt, no-impact with the preserved invariant, or decision-needed and stop dependent work. Keep correct sources unchanged and preserve user edits. Acceptance changes require a separate owner approval; never change an expectation to excuse a failure.

Commit reviewed implementation first. Prepare .bstack/assessment.json against that implementation commit and explicit base using the bundled evidence schema; include reviewed coverage and bind the current fingerprint. Commit only that assessment afterward. Keep execution captures outside product scopes. The selected first-contract foundation finding and its protected-write record must be retained in the assessment. The assessment is the explicit review record, not an activity log.

Run the complete dependency-free checker from this checkout:

```sh
node .bstack/bin/bstack-check.mjs --repo . --base <ancestor-commit> --assessment .bstack/assessment.json --json
```

It validates assessment coverage, runs required native checks freshly, then revalidates. Run it again in a different-root clean clone with an isolated home and cache and the same base and committed assessment. Failed, missing or stale evidence leaves the change unverified. Contract/checker changes preserve previous coverage or require a reviewed migration.

The versioned docs/repo-audit.md is a historical snapshot of its stated observed revision. It is not a live readiness authority. Keep final current-head findings and readiness evidence in scratch rather than rewriting that snapshot after each checker invocation. A later user edit requires fresh affected evidence and impact review.
